newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court releases Greenpeace activists.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court releases Greenpeace activists.

text.p: A Turkish court has released 18 Greenpeace activists, detained during a Friday demonstration at a thermal power plant in western Turkey, a local security official said on Saturday.
"Yesterday, they were taken to the court and the court released them. They are not here (under detention) now," said the gendarme official in the town of Milas.
Anatolian news agency said the activists, including 10 foreigners, held a demonstration on Friday to urge the government to close Kemerkoy power plant.
The demonstrators had chained themselves to the power station's gates.
Turkey is running the plant as part of a trial production process despite a court order for its closure.

"Our aim is to close down all power plants operating on coal and show officials that the current energy policy is a dead end," Melda Keskin, energy campaign official from the Greenpeace Mediterranean Office, told Turkish Daily News.
She said the continued operation of the plant was "unlawful".
